title: Santa Lucia Region
text:
Santa Lucia
The Santa Lucia region provides a contrasting setting to my open-ocean and spawning-zone work, with its own planktonic and biogeochemical dynamics.
Here, I’m interested in: - How local physical forcing interacts with zooplankton community structure - Comparisons between coastal and offshore systems - How regional processes integrate with larger-scale circulation and ecosystem variability

title: Eel Breeding Zones
text:
Eel Breeding Zones
I’ve contributed to work on the biogeochemistry and ecology of eel breeding zones, focusing on the zooplankton communities that support these systems.
Themes include: - Isotope structure of zooplankton in eel spawning regions - Vertical and horizontal gradients in community composition - Links between physical structure, biogeochemistry, and eel breeding grounds
This work connects basin-scale circulation, and the fine-scale plankton ecology that underpins eel life history.

title: Research
CCE-LTER & Pyrosomes
text:
CCE-LTER & Pyrosomes
I work in the California Current Ecosystem (CCE-LTER) using a mix of shipboard measurements, long-term datasets, image classification, and ecological theory to understand how pyrosomes fit into the system.
My main questions include: - When and where do pyrosomes appear in the Southern California Bight and CCE-LTER region? - How do pyrosome “blooms” alter zooplankton community structure in a trait-based sense (feeding modes, body size, behavior)? - What are the consequences for carbon export, grazing, and energy flow when pyrosomes are present?
This work combines: - Long-term CCE-LTER and CalCOFI time series - Shipboard process cruises - Image-based zooplankton data and machine learning classifiers - Trait-based interpretations of community change

title: Grace Cawley
text:
Welcome to my website, I’m Grace!
Zooplankton Ecologist | Biogeochemist
PhD Candidate | Décima Lab | Scripps Institution of Oceanography
Hey there! I’m a zooplankton ecologist who uses, shipboard measurements, isotopic tracers and machine-learning tools to understand how changing ocean conditions reshape pelagic food webs and biogeochemical cycling. I’m currently exploring the ecological significance and environmental drivers of pyrosomes in the Southern California Bight. Another key aim of my work is to understand how the presence of pyrosomes, along with shifting ecosystem dynamics in the California Current Ecosystem (CCE), is influencing zooplankton communities, with an emphasis on trait-based group shifts.
Additionally, I am working on a project investigating how mixotrophy influences energy transfer through the food web, and the zooplankton dynamics of the the Bluefin Tuna Spawning region in the Indian Ocean. I have also contributed to research on the biogeochemistry of eel breeding zones, including the isotope structure of the zooplankton communities and their abundances.
For my master’s degree at the University of San Diego, I focused on using isotope measurements and gut pigment analysis to determine copepod grazing on marine snow.

title: Bluefin Tuna Spawning Region (BLOOFINZ)
text:
Bluefin Tuna Spawning Region (BLOOFINZ)
In the bluefin tuna spawning region of the Indian Ocean, I’m interested in how mixotrophy and zooplankton dynamics shape energy transfer through the food web.
Focus areas: - The role of mixotrophic protists and their impact on apparent trophic position - How zooplankton biomass and traits structure potential prey fields for bluefin tuna larvae - How biogeochemistry and physical structure (fronts, eddies) interact with community composition
Methods include: - Bulk and compound-specific isotope analyses - Zooplankton community composition and size structure - Conceptual and trait-based food web models
